Panels \textbf{A--C} are an exact static quadratic consequence and numerical verification, not a temporal neural model. Panel \textbf{D} is a cross-study interpretation rather than a reanalysis of the original motor-learning data.
S7: \textbf{The fixed spatial map changes forward input coverage.} All panels use depth-four regular directed \([2,2,2,2]\) trees with 16 terminal branches. The spatial and random conditions differ only in which input coordinates reach those terminal branches; if an effect persists under backpropagation, it is a forward sparsity prior rather than a local-credit effect. \textbf{A}, Example contacts from one neuron. The map has the same number of contacts in both conditions but greater unique coverage and no cross-branch collisions in the spatial condition; its performance effect is therefore not specific to local credit assignment. Table~\ref{tab:spatial_coverage} gives the map coverage and overlap values.

S13: \textbf{A state-matched positive conductance approximates the predicted fixed-step branch-reliability factor, with a bounded training benefit.} This synthetic positive-rate task has eight parallel, nonserial branch blocks with heterogeneous signal and noise. It tests reliability-dependent gain and is not a reconstructed-arbor or physical-depth experiment. \textbf{A}, A nonnegative shunt $\kappa_b$ is paired with compensating current $\kappa_bV_b$, preserving branch voltage while reducing physical input resistance and local eligibility. \textbf{B}, Prescribed reliability profile $\min\{1,S_b/[c(S_b+N_b)]\}$ at maximum heterogeneity with $c=0.5$; \(S_b\) and \(N_b\) are branch signal and noise energies. SNR denotes signal-to-noise ratio. \textbf{C}, Mean one-step held-out loss decrease across 50 paired seeds for aligned, global, shuffled, anti-aligned, unshunted and exact clean-backpropagation (BP) rules. Lines and shading show seed means and 95\% paired-seed bootstrap intervals. \textbf{D}, Aligned-minus-global and aligned-minus-no-shunt one-step contrasts. At heterogeneity two, the former is positive in 49/50 seeds; the latter has a positive mean interval, is positive in 33/50 seeds and has two-sided Wilcoxon $P=0.0030$. \textbf{E}, Held-out loss after 40 updates. Exact clean backpropagation is the unattenuated optimization reference. \textbf{F}, Paired final-loss contrasts at maximum heterogeneity, displayed as control minus aligned so positive values favor aligned shunting. Aligned shunting beats the global, shuffled and anti-aligned shunts but has no reliable final difference from the unshunted noisy rule. The independently computed explicit point-gain control receiving the same sample-dependent factors agrees to numerical precision. All input rates and excitatory and shunt conductances are nonnegative. The oracle state clamp and fixed reliabilities isolate mechanism; they do not constitute autonomous shunt learning.
S14: \textbf{Same address span produces a finite-data coefficient-learning crossover.} A balanced tree indexes 16 abstract coefficient coordinates; no forward dendritic neuron is simulated. \textbf{A}, Orthonormal Haar, redundant nested and statically scaled nested dictionaries parameterize the identical rank-eight route span. \(\Phi\) is the dictionary and \(P_\Phi\) its projector; \(\Phi^\mathsf T\Phi\) is the Gram matrix. \textbf{B}, Positive Gram eigenvalues normalized to the largest, \(\lambda_j/\lambda_1\); condition numbers are 1, 15 and 388.52. \textbf{C,D}, Mean population-loss trajectories under common noisy local target estimates at effective sample sizes 4 and 256. Shading shows 95\% paired-seed bootstrap intervals across 50 seeds. At low data, slow nested modes filter variance; at high data, their retained bias dominates. \textbf{E}, Final loss across the sample-size series. \textbf{F}, Paired raw-nested-minus-Haar and scaled-nested-minus-Haar loss contrasts; negative values favor the nested coordinates. Solid points and bars are observed means and intervals; dashed curves are the exact finite-time risk from Eq.~\ref{eq:s_coefficient_finite_risk}. The reversal is a bias--variance effect within one span. The equality note in \textbf{A} reports that Gram-preconditioned controls make all parameterizations agree to $1.15\times10^{-15}$ and do not assert a biological implementation of the preconditioner.

They test the prerequisite for the main hypothesis: whether the mechanism-matched divisive task is accessible at every depth before comparing depth benefits. \textbf{A}, The original aligned shunting-backpropagation (BP) pilot at signal contrast 0.24 fit the training distribution increasingly with depth but remained at chance under the prespecified severe gain shift (test gain standard deviation (SD) 1.2). The separately run 0.80 boundary (dotted line) met the predefined accessibility criterion and selected the operating point used for the analysis seeds. Lines show two-seed means; shading spans the two exploratory values and is not a confidence interval. All pilot, ladder and boundary seeds were excluded from the confirmatory contrasts.
S16: \textbf{Initialization scores locate conditional route optima.} Panels \textbf{A--C} use the abstract 16-coordinate balanced-tree credit-operator experiment; the tree indexes Haar credit modes and is not a forward dendritic morphology. Panel \textbf{D} is a separate reanalysis of the trained eight-stream subtree-address factorial from main Fig.~3. \textbf{A}, Mean final population loss across routed depth $D_{\mathrm{r}}$ for task depths $H_{\mathrm c}=1$--$4$ in the hierarchy-depth routing experiment (aligned tree, $n=50$ seeds); open circles mark the loss minimum. \textbf{B}, Mean initialization utility (Supplementary Eq.~\ref{eq:s_projector_utility}) for the same conditions; open circles mark the utility maximum.
